question: What does standardization do mathematically, and what is the intuition behind it?
direct_answer: It subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation, so each feature is measured in units of its own spread.
expanded_answer: Standardization transforms a value by removing the feature’s average offset and then rescaling by typical variation. Subtracting the mean recenters the feature around zero. Dividing by the standard deviation makes a one-unit change mean “one standard deviation” rather than one raw unit. This gives features a common scale, which is especially helpful when the model depends on relative variation rather than raw units.
key_points: Rescale by dividing by standard deviation
common_wrong_ideas: Standardization always makes the distribution Gaussian
